reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Practice of optometry and included activities
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1 and subdivisions (1)-(10): non-exclusive ('includes, but is not limited to') definition of practice of optometry; sub (4) excludes injectable pharmaceutical agents. 1972 Dale Curteman annotation addresses contact-lens prescription and fitting.

headings.title: Optometrist surgery and laser prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: prohibits optometrists from performing surgery, including laser use for disease/condition treatment or refractive-error correction.

headings.title: Definitions used in this chapter
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3 and subdivisions (1)-(8): defines eye, adnexa, board, diagnostic/therapeutic/general pharmaceutical agents (excluding injectables in therapeutic), low vision care, and vision therapy (source spells 'regiment'), except as context requires.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.010 (bid 17941), all three subsections with subdivisions, history (RSMo 1939 § 10113 through A.L. 2007 merged bills), and 1972 case annotation (State ex inf. Danforth v. Dale Curteman, Inc., 480 S.W.2d 848). All three draft titles accurately reflect scope, non-exclusive list, surgery/laser bar, and chapter definitions; retained source spelling 'regiment' in sub 3(8).

headings.title: Optional fingerprint requirement for licensure applications
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: permissive authority ('may require') for the board to require fingerprint submissions with optometrist license applications under §§ 336.010 and 336.030.

headings.title: Fingerprint submission to highway patrol if required
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: conditional on board requirement under sub 1, applicants must submit fingerprints to the Missouri state highway patrol for state and federal background checks.

headings.title: Fingerprint routing, results, and record access
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: fingerprints and required fees go to the highway patrol central repository and FBI under § 43.540; patrol notifies board; records are accessible to board notwithstanding § 610.120.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.025 (bid 57246), all three subsections, and history note (L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174). Verified permissive 'may require' in sub 1, conditional trigger in sub 2, and highway patrol/FBI routing plus § 610.120 override in sub 3. Retained all three titles.

headings.title: Qualifications for optometrist license
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1(1)-(2): requires graduation from a board-approved optometry school plus either board-approved exam with pharmaceutical certification or 3-of-5-year licensed practice with pharmaceutical certification in a substantially equivalent jurisdiction (plus any required practical/Missouri-law exam).

headings.title: Board rules on examination and certification
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: permissive authority ('may adopt reasonable rules and regulations') for examination and certification of applicants to practice optometry.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.030 (bid 48441), both subsections with subdivisions, and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 10115 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046). Verified cumulative graduation requirement plus exam or reciprocity-practice routes (with pharmaceutical certification) and permissive rulemaking in sub 2. Retained both titles.

headings.title: License renewal, continuing education, and expiration
headings.reviewNote: Revised title to remove inaccurate 'Annual' and include expiration. Verified sub 1: active optometrists must renew by the renewal date with fee and 32 hours CE over the preceding two-year reporting period (including 2 hours Missouri jurisprudence), with board waiver for illness/good cause, in-state availability safeguard, and expiration if unrenewed.

headings.title: Renewal after expiration within five years
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: expired license may be renewed within five years upon paying reactivation fee and showing 48 hours of board-approved CE (or equivalent) during the five years.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.080 (bid 48442), both subsections, and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 10120 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046). Revised sub 1 title from 'Annual renewal and continuing education' to 'License renewal, continuing education, and expiration' because sub 1 does not specify annual renewal (it references a two-year CE reporting period and renewal date) and includes license expiration.

headings.title: Board refusal to issue license; applicant notice
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: board 'may' refuse licensure for sub 2 causes, and must notify applicant in writing of reasons and right to file a chapter 621 AHC complaint.

headings.title: Board complaint grounds against current and former holders
headings.reviewNote: Revised title to capture non-renewed and surrendered holders. Verified sub 2 and all 16 causes: board 'may' file a chapter 621 AHC complaint; includes § 324.012 criminal-offense standard and advertising exceptions in (14)(c)-(d).

headings.title: Hearing proceedings and board discipline limits
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: chapter 621 proceedings; upon AHC finding of grounds, board 'may' singly or in combination censure, place on probation up to 5 years, suspend up to 3 years, or revoke.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.110 (bid 48443), all three subsections including all 16 subdivisions and advertising exceptions (14)(a)-(d), and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 10121 through A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046). Preserved permissive 'may' framing and discipline limits; revised sub 2 title from 'Grounds for complaint against license holders' to 'Board complaint grounds against current and former holders' to reflect lapsed and surrendered licensees.

headings.title: Court injunctions on board application
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1(1)-(2): upon board application and required showing, a court of general jurisdiction 'may' enjoin unlicensed practice or practice by a licensee posing a serious danger to health, safety, or welfare.

headings.title: Venue for injunction actions
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: action must be commenced in the county where the conduct occurred or where the defendant resides.

headings.title: Injunction in addition to other penalties
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: injunction action is in addition to, not in lieu of, other chapter penalties and may be brought concurrently with other enforcement actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.115 (bid 17951), all three subsections with subdivisions (1)-(2), and source note (L. 1999 H.B. 867). Verified permissive court authority, venue rule, and cumulative-remedy clause. Retained all three titles.

headings.title: Board appointments, qualifications, terms, vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: governor appoints 6 members (5 optometrists with 5+ years experience, 1 voting public member) with senate consent; citizenship/residency, school/industry ineligibility, 5-year terms, removal upon ceasing active practice (except public member), vacancies, and oath.

headings.title: Public member qualifications and limits
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: public member citizenship/residency/voter and conflict-free criteria, selection of all members from division director lists, and exclusion of public member from technical licensure/competence determinations.

headings.title: Election of board officers
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: board members meet and organize by electing a president, vice president, and secretary.

headings.title: Officer duties, proceedings rules, and seal
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: board prescribes officer duties, adopts proceedings rules not inconsistent with chapter 336, and adopts a seal.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: rules effective only if compliant with chapter 536 and § 536.028 if applicable; repeals pre-August 28, 1999 rulemaking delegations while preserving compliant prior rules; nonseverable with chapter 536 legislative review powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.130 (bid 17953), all five subsections, and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 10110 through A.L. 1999 H.B. 343). Verified board composition, conflicts/ineligibility, public-member limits, officer/seal rules, and August 28, 1999 rulemaking/nonseverability clause. Retained all five titles.

headings.title: Meetings, compensation, and Optometry Fund
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: semiannual meetings with 10-day public notice, additional meetings with chapter 610 notice, up to $50/day compensation plus necessary expenses, and fee deposit into the Optometry Fund for chapter administration.

headings.title: Fund transfer to general revenue limits
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: notwithstanding § 33.080, Optometry Fund balance does not transfer to general revenue unless biennium-end balance exceeds 2x (or 3x if renewal is less frequent than yearly) prior fiscal year appropriation; only the excess lapses.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.140 (bid 17954), both subsections, and history notes (RSMo 1939 § 10112 through A.L. 2008 S.B. 850). Verified meeting notice, compensation cap, Optometry Fund creation, and § 33.080 general-revenue transfer thresholds. Retained both titles.

headings.title: Board duties, records, quorum, and bylaws
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: application review, certificates, prosecutions, annual governor report, bylaws, registration book, special meetings called by president, 3-member quorum, and public inspection. Notes include 1954 Brackman (quo warranto) and 1963 Ketring v. Sturges annotations.

headings.title: Rule effectiveness under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: no rule or portion of a rule under chapter 336 becomes effective unless promulgated pursuant to § 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.150 (bid 17955), both subsections, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 10111 through A.L. 1995 S.B. 3), and 1954 (Brackman) and 1963 (Ketring v. Sturges) case annotations. Retained both titles.

headings.title: Board rules and personnel
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: board 'may' adopt reasonable rules within chapter scope and 'may' employ board personnel (per § 324.001(11)(4)) as deemed necessary within appropriations.

headings.title: Fee setting by rule
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: board sets authorized/required fees by rule under § 536.021 at levels not substantially exceeding chapter administration costs. 1963 Ketring v. Sturges annotation in notes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.160 (bid 36053), both subsections, history notes (RSMo 1939 § 10125 through A.L. 2018 S.B. 975 & 1024 Revision), and 1963 case annotation (Ketring v. Sturges, 372 S.W.2d 104). Verified permissive rulemaking/personnel authority and § 536.021 cost-recovery fee limit. Retained both titles.

headings.title: Pharmaceutical certification requirement
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 1: notwithstanding § 336.010(1), uncertified optometrists remain prohibited from administering, dispensing, or prescribing diagnostic or therapeutic agents without an approved course and board certification; noted on license at each renewal.

headings.title: Physician referral for diagnostic-only optometrists
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 2: diagnostic-only optometrists must refer to a chapter 334 physician when exam indicates need for medical treatment, further diagnosis, or further refraction, except for known/previously diagnosed conditions; referral note has business-record standing; violations subject to § 336.110.

headings.title: Dispensing therapeutic agent prescriptions
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 3: therapeutic pharmaceutical prescriptions are dispensed by chapter 338 pharmacists; when dispensed by an optometrist, § 338.059 applies.

headings.title: Standard of care for pharmaceutical use
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 4: certified optometrists are held to the same standard of care in pharmaceutical diagnosis and treatment as physicians licensed by the healing arts board.

headings.title: Board rules for pharmaceutical certification
headings.reviewNote: Verified sub 5: permissive authority ('may adopt reasonable rules and regulations') for examination and certification of optometrists applying for pharmaceutical authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read archived § 336.220 (bid 17960), all five subsections, and history notes (L. 1981 S.B. 91 through A.L. 2007 merged bills). Verified certification mandate notwithstanding § 336.010(1), diagnostic-only referral rule and known-condition exception, chapter 338/§ 338.059 dispensing rules, physician standard of care, and permissive rulemaking. Retained all five titles.
